text:
mike: Quick thread — results from last night's 50k-concurrency runner. p99 tail spikes after ~90s, GPU util hits ~94% then latency climbs. attaching profiler snippet.
anya: can you paste the profiler top lines here? :thinking:
mike: sure — pasted below.
```
run_id: loadtest-2026-03-17
requests: 50k over 10m
avg_batch_size: 6.2
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
gpu_util_pct: 92-95 (90s spike)
kernel_switches_per_req: 1.8
median_latency_ms: 48
p95_latency_ms: 120
p99_latency_ms: 420 (tail surge after 90s)
long_context_fraction: 0.11 (>1024 tokens)
observed_drops: 0.4% (soft shed)
regression_after_pr: PR#4123 kernel reorder -> p99 +35% for long contexts
```
lin: interesting — kv_hit_rate only 62% which means lots of kvmiss work under pressure. that plus kernel switch churn could be causing the tail.
tom: did this test use the new microbatch sizing heuristic? we shifted target_microbatch=8 in canary config last night.
mike: yes, microbatch target was 8. actual avg was 6.2 (so underfilled). we also enabled kernel prefetch for kv hits but it only helps when hit_rate >0.8.
nikhil: hypothesis: high util -> longer queueing when microbatches underfill -> we see long tail for requests that miss KV and hit expensive kernel fallback. plus kernel swap has overhead.
sofie: ops suggestion: reduce target util to 82% for canary and add soft-admit to shed a small percent of long-context requests to lower p99. we tested soft admit in sim; looked promising.
anya: can we quantify tradeoff? what's the expected throughput loss vs p99 improvement?
mike: quick sim numbers: at util target 92% -> throughput baseline 1.00, p99 420ms. at target 82% -> throughput ~0.87, p99 ~180-210ms. soft-admit 2% long-context drop -> extra p99 improvement to ~160ms. overall token throughput down ~10-14% depending on traffic shape.
lin: i'd rather try adaptive admission: permit up to 88% util for short-ctx requests and cap long-ctx at 70% headroom. that keeps most traffic fast and protects tail.
tom: config draft for soft/adaptive admit (very small snippet):
```
admission:
  mode: adaptive
  global_util_target: 0.88
  short_ctx_util_target: 0.90
  long_ctx_util_target: 0.70
  long_ctx_threshold_tokens: 1024
  soft_shed_pct_long: 2.0
  max_queue_ms: 45
```
```
Deploy notes: canary rollout with route fallback to kernel=v1 (old) for requests >1024 tokens if p99 crosses 250ms for 5m window.
```
deploy-bot: started canary deploy redwood-runtime/canary/2026-03-18 at 02:10 UTC
```
nikhil: other mitigation: improve kv warmup by prefetching likely keys for in-progress sessions — increases hit_rate to ~0.78 in sim and reduces kernel fallback frequency.
sofie: action items: 1) mike to run 2 canaries: (A) util target 82% + soft-admit, (B) adaptive admission config above. 2) lin to add KV prefetch experiment toggles. 3) tom to prepare rollback plan to pin kernel=v1 for long contexts. 4) monitoring: add p95/p99 by ctx-length bins and kernel_switch_count histograms. expected timeline: run overnight, review morning.
mike: will run both canaries tonight and post raw logs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sofie: if canary A reduces throughput too much we'll prefer B + prefetch. keep an eye on customer-facing error rate.
anya: this is great — short-term knee: lower util + soft-admit. medium-term: improve kv hit and reduce kernel_switch cost. long-term: look at kswap elimination in runtime.
mike: noted, posting links to test dashboards when available: https://grafana.internal/r/loadtest-2026-03-17
